title: The Leaky Leaderboard

scenario.situation: After 200 hyperparameter-tuning trials all selected by test-set score, your model sits at the top of the internal leaderboard. But when it ships to production, live accuracy is noticeably worse than the test score promised.
scenario.stakeholderBelief: The team is convinced this is simply the best model they have ever built — the leaderboard score proves it.
scenario.question: Why is live performance so much worse, and can the leaderboard score be trusted?

decisions.prompt: The team insists the leaderboard score is solid. How do you frame your investigation into the production gap?

options.label: Diagnose the production pipeline for data drift
options.detail: Audit feature distributions and preprocessing steps between training and serving to look for a pipeline bug.
options.consequence: You find minor distribution shifts but nothing that explains a gap of this magnitude. The pipeline audit was a reasonable first step but it anchors on an implementation problem rather than an evaluation problem, so the real cause stays hidden.
options.divergenceCost: Anchored on a deployment explanation and missed the evaluation flaw entirely.

options.label: Counterfactual holdout audit — score the model on data the tuning loop never touched
options.detail: Set aside the tuning history and evaluate the final model on a completely locked partition that was never used to pick any trial.
options.consequence: You now have two numbers side by side: the score from the test set the tuner saw hundreds of times, and a score from data it never saw. If they diverge sharply, the evaluation process itself is the bug — not the model, not the pipeline.

options.label: Collect more training data and retrain
options.detail: Assume the model is underfitted to real-world variance; gather more labeled examples and run another tuning sweep.
options.consequence: More data helps marginally, but the new sweep is evaluated on the same test set — the core problem recurrs and the gap persists. You've burned time and budget without touching the root cause.
options.divergenceCost: Jumped to a solution before diagnosing the evaluation flaw.

options.label: Benchmark the winning model against a simpler baseline on the same test set
options.detail: Compare the tuned model to a logistic regression using the existing leaderboard metric.
options.consequence: The complex model still beats the baseline on the test set — which confirms the team's belief and reinforces the wrong conclusion. The contaminated metric validates both models equally poorly.
options.divergenceCost: Used a contaminated metric as the judge, making it impossible to see the real problem.

decisions.prompt: You pull the score history for all 200 trials. Which metric view do you trust to confirm what happened?

artifact.title: Model accuracy by trial milestone — test-set score (the tuner's objective)
artifact.caption: Test-set score climbs steadily with each tuning round. Live performance tells a very different story — but is the climb real learning or test-set memorization?

options.label: Test-set accuracy across the 200 tuning trials
options.detail: Plot the winning test-set score at each trial milestone to confirm the model improved over time.
options.consequence: The chart shows a clean upward curve — compelling evidence of progress. But every data point in this chart was also a vote that shaped which trial 'won.' The metric is both the judge and the defendant; it cannot convict itself.
options.divergenceCost: Relied on the same contaminated signal the tuner was already optimizing — circular validation.

options.label: Locked holdout accuracy vs. test-set accuracy, aligned by trial
options.detail: Evaluate every trial checkpoint on the locked holdout the tuner never saw, then plot both curves together.
options.consequence: The two curves start together, then diverge sharply: test-set accuracy keeps climbing while holdout accuracy plateaus around trial 40 and drifts back down. The model didn't keep getting better — it kept getting better at the test set specifically. The gap is adaptive overfitting made visible.

artifact.title: Accuracy by trial milestone — test-set score vs. locked holdout score
artifact.caption: After ~trial 50 the curves diverge. Holdout accuracy peaks early and erodes while test-set score keeps climbing — the signature of adaptive overfitting to the evaluation set.

decisions.prompt: The holdout curve diverges from the test-set curve after ~50 trials. What do you tell the team?

options.label: "The tuning loop overfitted to the test set — discard this model and retrain with a proper holdout."
options.detail: Make the causal call and prescribe an immediate fix.
options.consequence: You're probably right about the mechanism, but declaring the model worthless overstates what you've proven. The team may dismiss the finding as too aggressive. You've also skipped recommending a process change, so the same mistake can recur on the next project.
options.divergenceCost: Overclaimed certainty and prescribed action without a verification step or process safeguard.

options.label: "The test-set score inflated with each tuning round while the locked holdout plateaued — a pattern consistent with adaptive overfitting. Before we act, let's confirm with a fresh labeled sample, then adopt a locked final holdout as standard practice going forward."
options.detail: Present the finding, name the likely mechanism, flag the remaining uncertainty, and recommend both a verification step and a structural process fix.
options.consequence: You've given the team a falsifiable explanation, a concrete next step to verify it, and a process change that prevents recurrence. The finding lands without overreach, and the team has a clear path to a trustworthy leaderboard.

insight: The model never truly improved after the first ~50 trials — it learned the test set's idiosyncrasies one selection at a time, a process called adaptive overfitting. The leaderboard score was real arithmetic applied to a compromised evaluation protocol. The lesson is structural: a test set that participates in model selection stops being a test set; only a locked holdout the search never sees can give an honest estimate of generalization.
